clue.text: Oscar sails around with a Native American tribe

definitions.note: the answer is plural, naming the members of the tribe

indicators.note: to go around something is to encircle it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
jibs are triangular sails at the front of a boat
W is the standard abbreviation for with
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Oscar goes sailing with a group of Native Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: Oscar sounds like a person's name, but it is the phonetic-alphabet letter. The sails open up between their last two letters to take in W and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ojibwa are an Algonquian people of the Great Lakes region, so the plural names members of that tribe.

clue.text: Article about old British plane safeguards

indicators.note: whatever safeguards something keeps it protected inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: O is the usual abbreviation for old
B is the abbreviation for British
a jet is an aeroplane
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A newspaper article discusses an old British aircraft and the safety features it carries.
explanation.walkthrough: Article looks like the start of the wordplay (A or THE) but it is the definition. C for about comes from circa, as in dates like c.1900.
explanation.definitionFit: An object is a physical thing, just as an article can mean an item or thing, as in articles of clothing.

clue.text: Unorthodox scriptures, repeatedly exposed, increase suddenly

indicators.note: unorthodox means not following the accepted pattern, so the letters depart from their usual order
exposing strips off the outer covering, and doing it repeatedly peels away two layers of outside letters

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Heretical scriptures, exposed again and again, suddenly become far more widespread.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the ten letters as SC-IRRUPT-ES, then strip the outer letters twice: SC and ES go, leaving the six in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecologists say a population irrupts when its numbers rise sharply and abruptly, as with a plague of locusts.

clue.text: Female screws in battle attire

blocks.note: a war is a large-scale battle
dresses are items of attire

explanation.surface: Women dressed for combat, perhaps tightening screws on military hardware.
explanation.walkthrough: Screw is British slang for a prison officer, so the definition is not about fastenings at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardress is a female prison guard, and screws is British prison slang for such guards.

clue.text: Amazing Stories stored in disc I finalised

indicators.note: something stored in a container sits inside it, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the run of letters sits across these three words

explanation.surface: Someone has finished burning a collection of Amazing Stories onto a disc.
explanation.walkthrough: Amazing Stories, in italics, is the title of a famous American pulp magazine, the first devoted to the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazing Stories was a pioneering magazine of science fiction, so it stands as an example of the genre.

clue.text: Fool married – then sailed off

indicators.note: off here means gone wrong or out of place, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A foolish person got married and then promptly sailed away.
explanation.walkthrough: Fool looks like a noun for a silly person, but here it is a verb meaning to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: To mislead someone is to deceive them into a false belief, which is what fooling a person means.

clue.text: Supermodel circles capital in aircraft

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: Kate Moss is a famous British supermodel
Quito is the capital of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A supermodel flies in circles above a capital city in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: Aircraft serves as a plural here, matching the plural answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Mosquito was a famous British wooden combat plane of the Second World War.

clue.text: Preposterous feature of the Discovery Channel

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the letters form part of the words that follow
preposterous literally means before-behind in Latin, putting the end first, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: these letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Something ridiculous has been shown on the Discovery Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Channel looks like part of the TV station's name, but it is the definition; preposterous is used in its root sense of back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Side is dated British slang for a television channel, as in switching over to the other side.

clue.text: Secret coteries in new order

indicators.note: putting things in a new order means rearranging them, so the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Secretive cliques are being reorganised into a new order.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a secret society, which suits an answer meaning known only to insiders.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small inner circle, so it is effectively kept private and hidden.

clue.text: Remove slate deposit

blocks.note: to slate is to criticise harshly, which is to dis someone
to lodge money or a document is to deposit it

explanation.surface: Workers are clearing away a deposit of slate rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Slate and deposit look like geology nouns, but both are verbs: slate means criticise, deposit means lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to force it out of its fixed position, a way of taking it away.

clue.text: Magician with no trick to show panel member

indicators.note: having no share of something means lacking it, so some letters are taken away

blocks.note: a conjuror is a stage magician
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A magician without any tricks to perform appears on a TV talent panel.
explanation.walkthrough: The panel suggests a talent-show judge, but here it is a jury.
explanation.definitionFit: A juror sits on a jury, which is a panel of citizens sworn to decide a court case.

clue.text: Cunning, unpleasant son knocks out Victor

indicators.note: a boxer who knocks out a rival takes that rival's place in the ring, so one letter displaces another

blocks.note: invidious means unpleasant or likely to cause resentment
S is the abbreviation for son
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A crafty, nasty son punches out a man called Victor.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor looks like a man's name but is the phonetic-alphabet letter; the S goes into its slot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insidious works in a sly, stealthy way, spreading harm by guile, which is the crafty sense of cunning.

clue.text: Dissolute prince goes into business with American astronomer

indicators.note: dissolute means loose and disordered in morals, so the letters are loosened into a new order
to go into something is to enter it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: CO is short for company, a business
taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
US is short for American, as in US citizens

explanation.surface: A dissipated royal goes into partnership with an American stargazer.
explanation.walkthrough: The American looks like the astronomer's nationality, but it gives the closing letters; the astronomer alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicolaus Copernicus was the Polish Renaissance astronomer who placed the Sun at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: A run round US city

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: a and one are interchangeable, as in a hundred
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone goes for a jog around an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: Round looks like part of the jog, but it signals turning the letters back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Reno is a city in Nevada famous for its casinos and quick divorces, so it is an American urban centre.

clue.text: Grounds for replacing leader in state capital

indicators.note: to replace a leader is to swap out whoever is at the front, so the opening letter is exchanged

blocks.note: pro means in favour of, as in pros and cons
grounds for a belief are the evidence supporting it

explanation.surface: There are reasons for ousting the governor in a US state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Grounds for looks like a single phrase meaning reasons, but the two words are split: the second replaces the first letter of the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Providence is the capital city of Rhode Island, the smallest state in the United States.

clue.text: Bastard rats on old sod in government PR tactic

indicators.note: bastard can mean corrupted or not genuine, so the letters appear in a debased order

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
O is the usual abbreviation for old
sod is a piece of turf, grass with its roots and soil
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A furious insult aimed at a government spin doctor who informs on colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: Bastard and sod read as swear words, but one is an anagram signal and the other is grass turf; on just places the next pieces after the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Astroturfing means faking a grassroots campaign, a public-relations trick disguising organised messaging as spontaneous popular support.

clue.text: Take another look at king taking ecstasy with topless boyish young lady

indicators.note: to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another
topless means with the top removed, and in a down answer the top is the first letter

blocks.note: rex is Latin for king
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a gamine is a slim, boyish young woman

explanation.surface: A monarch on drugs is out with a boyish, bare-chested young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamine is a French borrowing for a slim, elfin young woman with boyish charm, like Audrey Hepburn; topless drops its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The prefix means again, and to examine is to inspect or study something closely, so together they mean looking a second time.

clue.text: Bust beginning to cause sexual excitement

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
arousal is a state of sexual excitement

explanation.surface: A glimpse of a bosom is the start of someone getting excited.
explanation.walkthrough: Bust looks like part of the body, but here it is the noun for a wild drinking spree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a spell of riotous drinking, the same as a carousal, a noisy boozy party or binge.

clue.text: Turned up to find primate dead after hosting Conference?

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside their home, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: an ape is a primate
Conference is a popular British variety of pear
D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone arrived to discover that an ape had died after hosting a conference.
explanation.walkthrough: Conference is capitalised and has a question mark because it is not a meeting but a British pear variety.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn up is to arrive or come into view, so appeared matches it in the past tense.

clue.text: Anxious nipper heaves up

indicators.note: things that are up are in turmoil or disorder, as when something is up, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nervous child is being sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Heaves up reads as a phrasal verb for vomiting, which hides that up is the anagram signal on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprehensive person feels worried or uneasy about what may happen, which is exactly being anxious.

clue.text: Poet, biblically, is going east

blocks.note: goeth is the King James Bible form of goes, or is going
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A poet with a Biblical turn of phrase is travelling eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Biblically tells the solver to use the old -eth verb ending found in the King James Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was the great German writer of Faust, and above all a celebrated lyric poet.

clue.text: Decline in large European city

blocks.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
Essen is a large industrial city in western Germany

explanation.surface: A big city in Europe is experiencing a downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Large looks like a description of the city, but it gives a single letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen is to become smaller or fewer, the intransitive sense of decline, as in shrinking numbers.

clue.text: Individuals with evaginated organ

indicators.note: evaginated means turned inside out, so the middle letters move to the edges and the edge letters move to the middle

blocks.note: the nose is the organ of smell

explanation.surface: People with a prolapsed body part, in medical jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: Turning the word inside out puts its middle pair outside and its outer pair in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ones can mean single persons or items, as in the little ones or loved ones, so it matches individuals.

clue.text: Linda Ronstadt's first poem translated into Malayalam?

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
translating turns text into a different form, so the letters are converted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the singer's surname supplies only its opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poem by the singer Linda Ronstadt is translated into the Indian language Malayalam.
explanation.walkthrough: Malayalam, a language of Kerala in India, looks like a translation target, but the question mark flags it as an example: it reads the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Malayalam spells the same forwards and backwards, making it an example of a word that reads identically in reverse.

clue.text: One nationalist has acquired some bullion?

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
N is the abbreviation for nationalist
has got means has acquired

explanation.surface: A patriot has managed to lay hands on a quantity of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that the definition is loose: an ingot is one piece of bullion rather than bullion itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingot is a cast bar of precious metal, and gold or silver held in bars is called bullion.

clue.text: Politician kidnapped by two black militants

indicators.note: someone kidnapped is held captive, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: II is the Roman numeral for two
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician has been abducted by a pair of armed radicals.
explanation.walkthrough: Two looks like a count of militants, but it is the Roman numeral that wraps around the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An impi was a Zulu regiment of warriors, so the word names a body of armed African fighters.

clue.text: Emulating the First Lady, Carol secures Conservative seat

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is gripped inside another

blocks.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the rump is the backside, what one sits on

explanation.surface: Copying a president's wife, a woman named Carol wins a Tory seat in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The First Lady is not a president's wife but Eve, the first woman, who took fruit from the forbidden tree; Carol is a verb, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrumping is British slang for stealing apples from an orchard, just as Eve plucked the forbidden fruit in Eden.

clue.text: Nathaniel's buttocks

blocks.note: Nate is the short form of the name Nathaniel
the possessive ending supplies its letter

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive reads as a label on Nathaniel's backside, but shorten the name and keep the ending to get the Latin word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nates is the anatomical Latin term for the buttocks, used in medicine for the rounded rear of the body.

clue.text: Job defender is less demanding after obtaining university degrees

indicators.note: having obtained something means now holding it, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: lite is an informal spelling of light, meaning easier or less demanding
U is the abbreviation for university
DD is the Doctor of Divinity degree, doubled here for the plural

explanation.surface: A trade unionist finds work easier after earning some academic qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: Degrees gives two Ds, one for each degree, placed after the university letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Luddites were 19th-century textile workers who smashed machines to protect their livelihoods from mechanisation.

clue.text: Spymaster leaves electronic instrument in that place

indicators.note: one who leaves goes away, so that letter departs from the word

blocks.note: M is the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories
the theremin is an early electronic instrument played without touching it

explanation.surface: The spy chief departs, leaving an electronic device behind at a secret location.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaves looks like leaves behind, but it means departs: the spymaster's letter goes out of the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Therein is a formal adverb meaning inside or within that thing, as in the problem lies therein.
